title: Polynomials & Rational Functions
description: Roots, polynomial division, linear factors, poles and asymptotes.
html:
📉 Polynomials & Rational Functions

1. Polynomials

$$p(x) = a_n x^n + \ldots + a_1 x + a_0, \quad a_n \neq 0$$

The end behaviour is determined by the leading term $a_n x^n$. Even degree: both ends the same direction; odd degree: opposite directions.

2. Roots and linear factors

$$p(a) = 0 \iff p(x) = (x - a)\,q(x)$$

  • A polynomial of degree $n$ has at most $n$ roots.
  • Integer roots (leading coefficient $1$) divide the constant term.
  • Odd multiplicity: the graph crosses the axis; even: it touches it.

3. Polynomial division and Horner

$$(x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6) : (x - 1) = x^2 - 5x + 6 = (x - 2)(x - 3)$$

Remainder theorem: the remainder on division by $(x - a)$ is $p(a)$. Horner's scheme: alternately multiply the coefficients by $a$ and add.

4. Rational functions

$$f(x) = \frac{p(x)}{q(x)}, \qquad D = \{x \mid q(x) \neq 0\}$$

Gaps and poles

Factorise and cancel: if the denominator factor also vanishes in the numerator → removable gap. Otherwise → pole (vertical asymptote).

Asymptotes ($x \to \pm\infty$)

  • deg numerator < deg denominator: $y = 0$
  • same degree: $y = \frac{a_n}{b_n}$
  • deg numerator = deg denominator $+ 1$: oblique asymptote via polynomial division
